passages.text: When Samuel grew old, he appointed his sons as judges over Israel.
passages.sermon: Samuel was a prophet and judge in Israel.\r\nSamuel grew old.\r\nSamuel appointed his sons as judges over Israel.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר זָקֵ֖ן שְׁמוּאֵ֑ל וַיָּ֧שֶׂם אֶת־ בָּנָ֛יו שֹׁפְטִ֖ים לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: The name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second was Abijah. They were judges in Beersheba.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet and judge in Israel.
Samuel had two sons.
His firstborn son was Joel.
His second son was Abijah.
Joel and Abijah served as judges.
They judged in the city of Beersheba.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י שֶׁם־ בְּנ֤וֹ הַבְּכוֹר֙ יוֹאֵ֔ל וְשֵׁ֥ם מִשְׁנֵ֖הוּ אֲבִיָּ֑ה שֹׁפְטִ֖ים בִּבְאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃

passages.text: But his sons did not walk in his ways; they turned aside toward dishonest gain, accepting bribes and perverting justice.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet and judge in Israel.
Samuel had sons.
His sons did not follow Samuel’s ways.
They turned aside to dishonest gain.
They accepted bribes.
They perverted justice.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ הָלְכ֤וּ בָנָיו֙ בְּדַרְכּוֹ וַיִּטּ֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֣י הַבָּ֑צַע וַיִּ֨קְחוּ־ שֹׁ֔חַד וַיַּטּ֖וּ מִשְׁפָּֽט׃פ

passages.text: So all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah.
passages.sermon:
The elders of Israel were the leaders of the people.
All the elders of Israel gathered together.
They came to Samuel.
Samuel was at Ramah.
passages.original: וַיִּֽתְקַבְּצ֔וּ כֹּ֖ל זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶל־ שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל הָרָמָֽתָה׃

passages.text: “Look,” they said, “you are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint a king to judge us like all the other nations.”
passages.sermon:
The elders of Israel spoke to Samuel.
They said, "You are old."
"Your sons do not walk in your ways."
"Appoint a king for us now."
"Let this king judge us."
"We want to be like all the other nations."
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו הִנֵּה֙ אַתָּ֣ה זָקַ֔נְתָּ וּבָנֶ֕יךָ לֹ֥א הָלְכ֖וּ בִּדְרָכֶ֑יךָ עַתָּ֗ה שִֽׂימָה־ לָּ֥נוּ מֶ֛לֶךְ לְשָׁפְטֵ֖נוּ כְּכָל־ הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

passages.text: But when they said, “Give us a king to judge us,” their demand was displeasing in the sight of Samuel; so he prayed to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet and judge in Israel.
The elders of Israel asked Samuel to appoint a king to judge them.
Their request displeased Samuel.
Samuel did not like their demand for a king.
Samuel prayed to the LORD.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֤רַע הַדָּבָר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמְר֔וּ תְּנָה־ לָּ֥נוּ מֶ֖לֶךְ לְשָׁפְטֵ֑נוּ וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֥ל שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל אֶל־ יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: And the LORD said to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of the people in all that they say to you. For it is not you they have rejected, but they have rejected Me as their king.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Samuel.
The LORD is God.
Samuel is a prophet and judge over Israel.
The LORD said, “Listen to the people.
Hear everything they say to you.
They have not rejected you, Samuel.
They have rejected Me.
I am their king.
They do not want Me to rule over them.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל שְׁמַע֙ בְּק֣וֹל הָעָ֔ם לְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ יֹאמְר֖וּ אֵלֶ֑יךָ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א אֹֽתְךָ֙ מָאָ֔סוּ כִּֽי־ אֹתִ֥י מָאֲס֖וּ מִמְּלֹ֥ךְ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Just as they have done from the day I brought them up out of Egypt until this day, forsaking Me and serving other gods, so they are doing to you.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Samuel.
God described the people of Israel.
God said He brought the people of Israel out of Egypt.
From that day until now, the people of Israel have turned away from God.
They have left God.
They have served other gods.
God said the people now treat Samuel the same way.
They reject Samuel, just as they rejected God.
passages.original: כְּכָֽל־ הַמַּעֲשִׂ֣ים אֲשֶׁר־ עָשׂ֗וּ מִיּוֹם֩ הַעֲלֹתִ֨י אֹתָ֤ם מִמִּצְרַ֙יִם֙ וְעַד־ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וַיַּ֣עַזְבֻ֔נִי וַיַּעַבְד֖וּ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים כֵּ֛ן הֵ֥מָּה עֹשִׂ֖ים גַּם־ לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Now listen to them, but you must solemnly warn them and show them the manner of the king who will reign over them.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Samuel.
God told Samuel to listen to the people.
The people wanted a king.
God told Samuel to do what the people asked.
God commanded Samuel to warn the people.
Samuel must give the people a serious warning.
Samuel must tell the people what the king will do.
Samuel must explain how the king will rule over them.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֖ה שְׁמַ֣ע בְּקוֹלָ֑ם אַ֗ךְ כִּֽי־ הָעֵ֤ד תָּעִיד֙ בָּהֶ֔ם וְהִגַּדְתָּ֣ לָהֶ֔ם מִשְׁפַּ֣ט הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִמְלֹ֖ךְ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: So Samuel spoke all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking him for a king.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of God.
The people of Israel asked Samuel for a king.
God gave Samuel a message.
Samuel spoke every word from God.
Samuel spoke to the people who wanted a king.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת כָּל־ דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אֶל־ הָעָ֕ם הַשֹּׁאֲלִ֥ים מֵאִתּ֖וֹ מֶֽלֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: He said, “This will be the manner of the king who will reign over you: He will take your sons and appoint them to his own chariots and horses, to run in front of his chariots.
passages.sermon:
Samuel spoke to the people.
Samuel told them what God said.
Samuel described the king who would rule over them.
The king will take your sons.
He will put your sons with his chariots.
He will put your sons with his horses.
Your sons will run in front of his chariots.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר זֶ֗ה יִֽהְיֶה֙ מִשְׁפַּ֣ט הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִמְלֹ֖ךְ עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם אֶת־ בְּנֵיכֶ֣ם יִקָּ֗ח וְשָׂ֥ם לוֹ֙ בְּמֶרְכַּבְתּ֣וֹ וּבְפָרָשָׁ֔יו וְרָצ֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י מֶרְכַּבְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He will appoint some for himself as commanders of thousands and of fifties, and others to plow his ground, to reap his harvest, to make his weapons of war, and to equip his chariots.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of the LORD.
Samuel spoke to the people of Israel.
The people of Israel asked Samuel for a king.
Samuel told them what the king would do.
The king will choose some men for himself.
He will make some men commanders over a thousand soldiers.
He will make some men commanders over fifty soldiers.
He will make some men plow his fields.
He will make some men gather his harvest.
He will make some men build his weapons for war.
He will make some men make equipment for his chariots.
passages.original: וְלָשׂ֣וּם ל֔וֹ שָׂרֵ֥י אֲלָפִ֖ים וְשָׂרֵ֣י חֲמִשִּׁ֑ים וְלַחֲרֹ֤שׁ חֲרִישׁוֹ֙ וְלִקְצֹ֣ר קְצִיר֔וֹ וְלַעֲשׂ֥וֹת כְּלֵֽי־ מִלְחַמְתּ֖וֹ וּכְלֵ֥י רִכְבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And he will take your daughters to be perfumers, cooks, and bakers.
passages.sermon:
The king will rule over you.
He will take your daughters.
He will make them perfumers.
He will make them cooks.
He will make them bakers.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ בְּנוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם יִקָּ֑ח לְרַקָּח֥וֹת וּלְטַבָּח֖וֹת וּלְאֹפֽוֹת׃

passages.text: He will take the best of your fields and vineyards and olive groves and give them to his servants.
passages.sermon:
A king will rule over you.
He will take the best of your fields.
He will take the best of your vineyards.
He will take the best of your olive groves.
He will give these to his servants.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ שְׂ֠דֽוֹתֵיכֶם וְאֶת־ כַּרְמֵיכֶ֧ם וְזֵיתֵיכֶ֛ם הַטּוֹבִ֖ים יִקָּ֑ח וְנָתַ֖ן לַעֲבָדָֽיו׃

passages.text: He will take a tenth of your grain and grape harvest and give it to his officials and servants.
passages.sermon:
A king will rule over you.
He will take a tenth of your grain.
He will take a tenth of your grape harvest.
He will give this portion to his officials.
He will give this portion to his servants.
passages.original: וְזַרְעֵיכֶ֥ם וְכַרְמֵיכֶ֖ם יַעְשֹׂ֑ר וְנָתַ֥ן לְסָרִיסָ֖יו וְלַעֲבָדָֽיו׃

passages.text: And he will take your menservants and maidservants and your best cattle and donkeys and put them to his own use.
passages.sermon:
A king will rule over you.
He will take your male servants.
He will take your female servants.
He will take your best young men.
He will take your donkeys.
He will use them for his own work.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ עַבְדֵיכֶם֩ וְֽאֶת־ שִׁפְח֨וֹתֵיכֶ֜ם וְאֶת־ בַּחוּרֵיכֶ֧ם הַטּוֹבִ֛ים וְאֶת־ חֲמוֹרֵיכֶ֖ם יִקָּ֑ח וְעָשָׂ֖ה לִמְלַאכְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will become his slaves.
passages.sermon: A king will rule over you.\r\nHe will take a tenth of your flocks.\r\nYou will become his slaves.
passages.original: צֹאנְכֶ֖ם יַעְשֹׂ֑ר וְאַתֶּ֖ם תִּֽהְיוּ־ ל֥וֹ לַעֲבָדִֽים׃

passages.text: When that day comes, you will beg for relief from the king you have chosen, but the LORD will not answer you on that day.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel chose a king for themselves.
One day, trouble will come because of this king.
On that day, you will cry out for help.
You will beg for relief from the king you chose.
The LORD will not answer you on that day.
passages.original: וּזְעַקְתֶּם֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא מִלִּפְנֵ֣י מַלְכְּכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּחַרְתֶּ֖ם לָכֶ֑ם וְלֹֽא־ יַעֲנֶ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃

passages.text: Nevertheless, the people refused to listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We must have a king over us.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel spoke to Samuel.
Samuel was a prophet and judge.
The people refused to listen to Samuel.
They said, “No.”
They said, “We must have a king over us.”
passages.original: וַיְמָאֲנ֣וּ הָעָ֔ם לִשְׁמֹ֖עַ בְּק֣וֹל שְׁמוּאֵ֑ל וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לֹּ֔א כִּ֥י אִם־ מֶ֖לֶךְ יִֽהְיֶ֥ה עָלֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Then we will be like all the other nations, with a king to judge us, to go out before us, and to fight our battles.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel spoke.
They wanted to be like all the other nations.
They wanted a king to rule over them.
They wanted a king to judge them.
They wanted a king to go out in front of them.
They wanted a king to fight their battles.
passages.original: וְהָיִ֥ינוּ גַם־ אֲנַ֖חְנוּ כְּכָל־ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וּשְׁפָטָ֤נוּ מַלְכֵּ֙נוּ֙ וְיָצָ֣א לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ וְנִלְחַ֖ם אֶת־ מִלְחֲמֹתֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Samuel listened to all the words of the people and repeated them in the hearing of the LORD.
passages.sermon: Samuel was a prophet and leader of Israel.\r\nSamuel listened to everything the people said.\r\nSamuel spoke all their words to the LORD.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת כָּל־ דִּבְרֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם וַֽיְדַבְּרֵ֖ם בְּאָזְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: “Listen to their voice,” the LORD said to Samuel. “Appoint a king for them.” Then Samuel told the men of Israel, “Everyone must go back to his city.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Samuel.
The LORD said, “Listen to the people.”
The LORD said, “Appoint a king for them.”
Samuel spoke to the men of Israel.
Samuel said, “Each man must return to his own city.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל־ שְׁמוּאֵל֙ שְׁמַ֣ע בְּקוֹלָ֔ם וְהִמְלַכְתָּ֥ לָהֶ֖ם מֶ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל־ אַנְשֵׁ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְכ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ לְעִירֽוֹ׃פ
